identity.title: ScaleCUA: Scaling Open-Source Computer Use Agents with Cross-Platform Data

problem.claim: Scale open-source computer-use agents that autonomously operate graphical user interfaces across platforms.

gap.claim: Progress is limited by the lack of large-scale, open-source computer-use data and foundation models.

contributions.claim: A dataset spanning 6 operating systems and 3 task domains, built through a closed-loop pipeline combining automated agents with human experts.
ScaleCUA, an open-source computer-use-agent scaling effort trained on the expanded cross-platform data.
The authors report cross-platform operation and improved benchmark results, including new stated state-of-the-art scores.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present ScaleCUA as a step toward scaling open-source computer-use agents through cross-platform data.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report gains over baselines of +26.6 on WebArena-Lite-v2 and +10.7 on ScreenSpot-Pro.
The authors report scores of 94.4% on MMBench-GUI L1-Hard, 60.6% on OSWorld-G, and 47.4% on WebArena-Lite-v2 as new state-of-the-art results.
The authors report that ScaleCUA operates seamlessly across platforms after training on the scaled-up data.

narrative_sequence.summary: GUI-capable computer-use agents show promise, but open-source data and foundation models remain scarce.
ScaleCUA is introduced with a cross-platform dataset covering 6 operating systems and 3 task domains, constructed using automated agents and human experts.
The authors report cross-platform operation, baseline gains, and stated state-of-the-art benchmark scores.
The findings are presented as evidence of the value of data-driven scaling for general-purpose agents, alongside a planned release of data, models, and code.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a concrete data-scaling description—operating-system and domain coverage plus pipeline design—with benchmark-specific gains and scores.

lessons.interpretation: This links the proposed resource to measurable outcomes while preserving the scope of the claimed evidence.
lessons.application: When presenting a scaling method, state the dimensions of data coverage and report improvements on named benchmarks with exact values.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when benchmark definitions, baselines, or comparable evaluation conditions cannot be specified.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify baseline systems, metric definitions, sample sizes, or evaluation conditions behind the reported gains and state-of-the-art claims.
It does not establish whether the announced data, models, and code have already been released.
